## 2026-11-08 - Fix: the monster's orbs broke clicking ("Invalid access to property 'click_radius' ... Orb")
- Reported: entering the monster's signal site gave "Invalid access to property or key 'click_radius' on a
  base object of type 'Node2D (Orb)'".
- Cause: SpaceMonster put its energy orbs in the Enemy's parent - the `enemies` node - and the click / hover
  picking (main._enemy_at) and other code walk that node's children as ships.
- Fix: the orbs go in the effects layer (group "fx_layer", like projectiles); never among the ships.
- Test: test_signals.test_wreck_and_monster - no orb among the enemies' children; picking where they fly
  works. 7 passed.
- Files: scripts/space_monster.gd, tests/test_signals.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Fix: followed NPC ships turned back and forth after a while
- Reported: following an NPC ship for over a minute, it "got confused", changing direction at random,
  going back and forth.
- Found (a probe following 5 neutrals for 90 s each): your ship kept ~240 behind throughout - it was the
  followed ships. Patrol warships (and pirates) wandered by picking a random point 100-450 from home each
  time they reached one, so they reversed every few seconds: 10-19 reversals in 90 s. Explorers picked any
  direction after each stop (2 reversals).
- Enemy._patrol: a circuit of 4-6 waypoints 700-1,400 round home (jittered), flown in order the same way
  round, joined at the nearest; next waypoint within 160. Explorers' next open-space point is ahead of them
  (their heading +-1.6 rad), not behind.
- After: 0-1 reversals in 90 s for every ship probed.
- Test: test_play.test_followed_ships_fly_steady - following a patrol ship and an explorer for 90 s each:
  at most 2 reversals, you stay within 450. 99 passed.
- Files: scripts/enemy.gd, tests/test_play.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Fix: dialogues kept the mouse; voices 50 % louder
- Asked: some main-quest dialogues seem to capture the mouse - they shouldn't; raise the voices' volume by 50 %.
- Cause (mouse): pressing the left button in empty space starts steering, which hides the cursor until the
  button is released. A story dialogue opening meanwhile (an objective reached, docking...) pauses the game
  and its dim backdrop takes the release - main never saw it, so the cursor stayed hidden.
- Fix: Dialogue.play releases steering (group "steering" -> main.release_steering: steering off, the ship
  stops) and shows the cursor; main._update_steering also ends steering whenever the left button isn't
  actually held (any panel that eats the release).
- Voices: tools/voice_lines.py levels to -14.5 LUFS (was -18: +3.5 dB = x1.5), true peak -1 dBFS (was -2) so
  nothing clips; all 78 lines re-recorded (--force; same keys). Measured -14.4..-16.2 LUFS (was -17.5..-18.9),
  peaks -0.4..0.0 dBFS - short lines gain a little less (their peaks set the limit).
- Test: test_play.test_dialogue_frees_the_mouse (press to steer, a dialogue opens: steering ends, the cursor
  visible). 100 passed.
- Files: scripts/dialogue.gd, scripts/main.gd, tools/voice_lines.py, voices/lines/*.ogg (78, re-recorded),
  external/voices/lines.md, tests/test_play.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Dying keeps your progress (Respawn); the title screen's attract mode
- Asked: dying should not reset the main quest and lose progress. And: left 30 s on the main menu, the game
  plays itself - the player driven round the solar systems, visiting planets etc. - with "Please insert
  drachma" slowly blinking in big bold gold text at the bottom (not over the UI); moving the mouse or
  clicking goes back to the main menu.
- Death: the game-over panel's Restart started a new game (SaveGame.pending = {}), throwing everything away.
  Now it's **Respawn** (hud.tscn button, tooltip): main.respawn() - respawn_state() is the current game
  (like a jump: SaveGame.pending + travelling, the galaxy kept) with a new ship (full hull / shields, no
  velocity) beside the nearest station, the system's pirates afresh, your cargo (Items.is_cargo) lost and
  RESPAWN_FEE 10 % of your credits paid as insurance; the main quest, missions, reputation, scenarios, planets'
  state and everything else as they were. Logged. (A new game: Main Menu > Start Game.)
- Attract mode (scripts/attract_mode.gd, new: AttractMode): main_menu.gd counts idle time on the title screen
  (any key / click / mouse movement resets it); at IDLE 30 s AttractMode.start() - a fresh game, active (a
  static) across scene changes. main.gd / planet_surface.gd add the controller while it's on:
  - Space: the ship invulnerable (Ship.invulnerable - take_damage / hazard_damage), zoomed out a little; an
    autopilot cycling tasks (each gives up after 22 s): fly to a planet and circle it (every third planet
    visit lands, if landable), circle a station, mine the nearest asteroid, a system scan every 4th task,
    through a gate to the next system every 7th; pirates within 900 are fought first. No gate prompt
    (_check_gates), no saving (can_save false), any dialogue that pops up is closed.
  - On a planet: walks to open spots 300-700 px away every 5-8 s, takes off after 35 s.
  - The banner: "PLEASE INSERT DRACHMA", 54 px emboldened gold with a dark outline and shadow, bottom centre
    above the toolbar (offset -205..-135, clear of the event log), blinking slowly (2.5 s, alpha 0.15..1).
  - Any key, click, joypad button or mouse movement over 6 px (after a 1.2 s grace) -> AttractMode.stop():
    back to the title screen.
- Checked end to end (a real window): the menu idle -> the game playing (a pirate fought, planets and
  stations visited), a mouse move -> the menu.
- Docs: game.md (Welcome: Respawn, the attract mode).
- Tests: test_play.test_respawn_keeps_progress (quest stage, missions, reputation kept; 10 % fee; cargo lost,
  kit kept; full hull at a station), test_play.test_attract_mode (driving, invulnerable, no saving, the
  banner placed and blinking). 102 passed.
- Files: new scripts/attract_mode.gd; changed scripts/main.gd, hud.gd, scenes/hud.tscn, ship.gd, dialogue.gd,
  main_menu.gd, planet_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_play.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Arcade Greek letters for "PLEASE INSERT DRACHMA"

Asked: the attract-mode banner should use a font very similar to the 80s arcade "INSERT COIN";
then: keep the arcade style, stylized to look like ancient Greek letters.

Done: the banner is now hand-drawn pixel lettering (inner class AttractMode.Banner, drawn with
draw_rect, no font file): 13 glyphs on the arcade 8 x 8 grid (7 x 7 used), 2-pixel strokes,
at 5 screen px per pixel. Faux-Greek forms: Λ for A, Σ for E, Δ for D, a squared S (like a
meander turn) and a squared C (lunate sigma); M splayed; the rest Greek capitals (Ρ, Ι, Ν, Τ, Η).
The 7 rows shade from pale gold to orange (arcade gradient) with a hard 5 px dark shadow, between
two meander (Greek key) bands of 3 px pixels, the lower one mirrored. About 835 x 130 px; clear of
the event log and toolbar at 1920x1080 and 1280x720. Still blinks slowly (2.5 s). (A Press Start 2P
font was tried first and dropped - nothing added to assets.) Was 54 px emboldened Noto with an outline.

Files: scripts/attract_mode.gd (_build_banner, class Banner); tests/test_play.gd (test_attract_mode checks every letter has a glyph).


## 2026-11-08 - CRT filter during attract mode

Asked: when autoplay (attract mode) is on, put a CRT with scanlines over the entire window for an old-school feel.

Done: new shaders/crt.gdshader (canvas_item, reads the screen texture) on a full-window ColorRect in
CanvasLayer 127 - over the game, HUD and the drachma banner, under the scene-change fades (128). The
AttractMode controller adds it in space and on planets, so it lives only while the demo runs and is gone
when you're back on the menu. Effects: curved tube (barrel warp 0.07) with rounded black corners;
scanlines every 3 screen px (38% dark between lines); RGB aperture-grille stripes (14%); colour
fringing growing to 1.2 px at the edges; a darker rim (vignette 0.32); a faint 60 Hz flicker and a slow
rolling bright band; brightness x1.2 to make up for the lines.

Files: shaders/crt.gdshader (new), scripts/attract_mode.gd (CRT_SHADER, crt, _build_banner),
tests/test_play.gd (test_attract_mode checks the CRT covers the window).

## 2026-11-08 - CRT filter in Settings, with its own page

Asked: make the CRT effect available in settings but disabled by default, expose all its parameters,
and if they are too many give it its own settings page. Then publish the patch.

Done:
- The filter moved out of attract mode into scripts/crt_filter.gd (class CrtFilter, CanvasLayer 127),
  which Settings adds to the root at startup so it covers every scene. It shows when "Always on" is set
  (default OFF), during attract mode when "In attract mode" is set (default ON - the earlier request),
  and while the CRT settings page is open (a live preview).
- Every shader parameter is now a uniform (flicker, roll and corner were constants) - 10 in all:
  curvature 0-0.2 (0.07), round corners 0-0.15 (0.035), scanline size 2-8 px (3), scanlines 0-100% (38%),
  phosphor mask 0-50% (14%), colour fringe 0-4 px (1.2), dark rim 0-100% (32%), brightness 60-180% (120%),
  flicker 0-6% (1.2%), rolling band 0-20% (4%). Settings.CRT_PARAMS lists them (range, step, default,
  display, tooltip); saved in settings.cfg [crt]; Restore Defaults resets them and the switches.
- Settings page: a new "CRT filter" row (switch + "Tune..." button); row spacing 16 -> 11 so Back still
  fits at 1080p (bottom 1061 px). "Tune..." opens the CRT FILTER page (too many for the main page): the two
  switches, a slider per parameter with value and reset button, "Default Look" (the sliders only) and
  Back; Esc goes back to Settings. Preview is cleared when the menu closes or is freed.
- Guide (Welcome) mentions the CRT filter.

Files: scripts/crt_filter.gd (new), shaders/crt.gdshader (all params uniforms), scripts/settings.gd
(CRT_PARAMS, crt_on/crt_attract/crt_preview/crt, set_crt, set_crt_switch, reset_crt, save/load),
scripts/main_menu.gd (CRT row, _build_crt_settings, page, Esc), scripts/attract_mode.gd (filter removed),
data/docs/game.md, tests/test_crt.gd (new, 3 tests), tests/test_play.gd (attract test uses CrtFilter).
